issues_detected.description: No software is named that produced or transformed the distributed data. The record states that Topcon .fda and Heidelberg .sdt files were converted to DICOM, Garmin .FIT files to Open mHealth, and ECG to WFDB, and that processing moved from 'custom or ad hoc' to 'automated plus custom', but names no converter, pipeline or library and populates no used_software on any strategy. The software actually named falls entirely into non-qualifying roles: capture and instrumentation (REDCap, MoCA Duo application, device vendor exports), hosting and serving (FAIRhub, Microsoft Azure), metadata production (RO-Crate 1.2-DRAFT, FAIRscape profile 0.1), and validation (OMOP CDM Data Quality Dashboard, dqd_omop.json). The GitHub pointer https://github.com/AI-READI is an organisation root that identifies only the publisher.
issues_detected.recommendation: Name the conversion and standardization software with versions (for example the .fda/.sdt-to-DICOM converter and the .FIT-to-Open-mHealth converter) and attach them via used_software on the relevant preprocessing_strategies entries, with repository or DOI links to the AI-READI processing code.

issues_detected.description: The accountable organization is unresolved across tier-1 sources: FAIRhub study metadata and the license name Washington University in St. Louis (ROR 01yc7t268) as lead sponsor, managing organization and Licensor, while the RO-Crate places the principal investigator in the Department of Ophthalmology at the University of Washington and the healthsheet and BMJ Open protocol place IRB oversight at the University of Washington. The record picks Washington University in St. Louis for data_governance.accountable_organization and the University of Washington for ethical_reviews.reviewing_organization, so the datasheet asserts both readings in different slots.
issues_detected.recommendation: Obtain the authoritative licensor and IRB-of-record attribution from the AI-READI Consortium and state which institution is accountable for governance versus which reviewed the protocol, rather than leaving the two slots divergent.

issues_detected.description: The variables list is explicitly a representative subset rather than the full inventory (a 'Representative subset marker' pseudo-variable is included to say so), and no variable carries a persistent or ontology identifier (no OMOP concept id, LOINC or similar) despite the clinical data being mapped one-to-one to OMOP CDM tables.
issues_detected.recommendation: Attach OMOP concept identifiers or LOINC codes to the laboratory and clinical variables and either enumerate the full inventory or reference the machine-readable data dictionary per domain rather than a prose pointer to docs.aireadi.org.

issues_detected.description: Internal arithmetic disagreement carried from the source: the nine datatype directory sizes sum to 3,815,969,360,064 bytes, 419,614 bytes short of the reported total_size_bytes of 3,815,969,779,678. The datasheet discloses the shortfall and states it is unexplained by the bundle.
issues_detected.recommendation: Reconcile the per-directory byte totals with the dataset total, or state what the residual accounts for (for example the nine root-level metadata files).

issues_detected.description: The deidentification account is internally tense: FAIRhub records deIdentificationType 'NoDeIdentification' (on the reasoning that no identifiers were ever collected) while the same block asserts HIPAA Privacy Rule Safe Harbor stripping of Protected Health Information and lists identifiers_removed. The record flags the tension and explains its basis.
issues_detected.recommendation: State the operative determination once (no identifiers collected, therefore Safe Harbor verified rather than applied) so downstream consumers do not read 'NoDeIdentification' as an absence of protection.

issues_detected.description: Two governance values are derived rather than quoted and the record says so: confidentiality_level 'restricted' is inferred from the access model while the RO-Crate's own term is 'HL7:2N (normal)', and hipaa_compliant 'compliant' is inferred because no source makes a compliance determination in those words.
issues_detected.recommendation: Retain the disclosure; where possible cite a source statement that classifies the release, so the enum value rests on an attestation rather than on an inference from the access workflow.

issues_detected.description: sensitive_elements carries two entries with opposite sensitive_elements_present values (false per the healthsheet for the public release, true per the RO-Crate rai:personalSensitiveInformation list). The record explains that the two sources enumerate different things (sensitive attributes versus data-source categories) and names the healthsheet reading as governing.
issues_detected.recommendation: Keep both readings but mark the RO-Crate entry as a data-source enumeration rather than a sensitivity assertion, so automated consumers do not read a contradiction.

issues_detected.description: The dedicated download_url slot is unpopulated; access links are carried in distribution_formats.access_urls (https://fairhub.io/datasets/3 and /access) and in page. Likewise data_governance.committee_contact is unpopulated, with contact routing given as prose in maintainers (contact@aireadi.org) and data_protection_impacts is absent though re-identification risk is assessed under participant_privacy.
issues_detected.recommendation: Populate download_url and data_governance.committee_contact from the values already present in prose, and record the re-identification risk assessment under data_protection_impacts as well as participant_privacy.

issues_detected.description: Unreconciled source figures are recorded rather than resolved in three places: the planned Year-4 follow-up fraction (10% per NIH RePORTER and the FAIRhub study description versus approximately 4% per the healthsheet), the project-name expansion ('Exploratory' versus 'Equitable' Atlas for Diabetes Insights), and the enrollment start date (2023-07-19 per FAIRhub versus 18 July 2023 per BMJ Open). Each is disclosed with the tie-break rule applied.
issues_detected.recommendation: No action required for evaluation purposes; the disclosures are exemplary. Resolve the follow-up fraction with the study team since it affects expectations for future longitudinal releases.

semantic_insights: DOI 10.60775/fairhub.3 is well formed and the 10.60775 prefix is the FAIRhub registrant, consistent with publisher https://fairhub.io/ and page https://fairhub.io/datasets/3 — identifier, platform and landing page corroborate each other.

Grant OT2OD032644 matches the NIH pattern for a Common Fund Other Transaction award (activity code OT2, institute OD), and the Bridge2AI Salutogenesis program attribution aligns semantically with purposes that name salutogenic pathways in T2DM.

Non-grant support is represented correctly: device loans (Topcon, Optomed, iCare, Carl Zeiss) and research discounts (Heidelberg, Dexcom, Garmin) and Microsoft AI for Good cloud support are recorded as funders without spurious grant numbers.

Instance and split arithmetic is fully self-consistent: 1,576 + 352 + 352 = 2,280; race/ethnicity 380+545+519+836 = 2,280; sex 951+1,329 = 2,280; diabetes status 776+560+686+258 = 2,280, and each split's own strata sum to its size.
File-count arithmetic reconciles exactly: the nine datatype directories sum to 356,334 files and the nine root-level metadata files account for the difference to the reported 356,343.
Temporal ordering is coherent: collection 2023-07-19 to 2025-05-01, release of v1.0.0 2024-05-03, v2.0.0 2024-11-08, v3.0.0 2025-11-17 with issued 2025-11-17 matching the described version.

HIPAA Safe Harbor is an appropriate deidentification method for prospectively collected clinical, imaging, waveform and wearable data, and the additional removal of sex, race/ethnicity and medications to a controlled tier is a coherent, stated rationale rather than boilerplate.

human_subject_research.involves_human_subjects=true is corroborated downstream by IRB protocol STUDY00016228 with an approval date, reliance agreements, written e-consent in REDCap, a withdrawal mechanism with its stated limit, and a $200 stipend with prorating and disbursement conditions.

is_tabular=false and instances.label=false are semantically consistent with a multimodal DICOM/WFDB/Open mHealth release that the description says ships without labels or targets, and with the absence of labeling_strategies.

Bias documentation is taxonomy-aligned (selection, sampling, representation, measurement) and each entry carries a mitigation that is actually responsive to the stated bias, including recommended splits balanced on the very attributes withheld from the public tier.

Access restrictiveness is internally aligned: restricted confidentiality, verified-ID self-attestation, disease-specific data_use_permission, prohibited_uses barring re-identification and third-party model training, and watermarking all point the same direction.

overall_score.denominator_note: normalized_percentage uses adjusted_max_points = 50; fixed_percentage uses max_points = 50. No sub-element was excluded, so the two bases coincide and no excluded item identities are reported.

elements.name: Dataset Discovery and Identification
elements.description: Can a user or system discover and uniquely identify this dataset?

sub_elements.evidence: doi: 10.60775/fairhub.3; id: doi:10.60775/fairhub.3; version_access.latest_version_doi: doi:10.60775/fairhub.3; prior versions doi:10.60775/fairhub.1 and doi:10.60775/fairhub.2
sub_elements.quality_note: A single resolvable DOI identifies this release, and the versioned DOI series makes the identified object unambiguous (the DOI names v3.0.0, not a moving target).
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Format matches 10.XXXX/...; prefix 10.60775 is the FAIRhub DataCite registrant, plausible and corroborated by publisher https://fairhub.io/ and page https://fairhub.io/datasets/3. No RRID is claimed, so RRID validation is not_present rather than failed.

sub_elements.name: Dataset Title and Description Completeness
sub_elements.evidence: title: 'Flagship Dataset of Type 2 Diabetes from the AI-READI Project'; description (~2,000 chars) gives 2,280 adults, three harmonized sites (UAB, UCSD, UW), collection 2023-07-19 to 2025-05-01, the modality inventory (OMOP clinical/survey, 12-lead ECG in WFDB, retinal photography/OCT/OCTA/FLIO in DICOM, CGM and wearable activity in Open mHealth, indoor environmental sensing), 356,343 files at ~3.82 TB, CDS v0.1.1 organization, and the public/controlled split of variables
sub_elements.quality_note: Far beyond the 200-character threshold and specific throughout: counts, dates, sites, formats, structure and what is withheld are all stated, so a reader can decide relevance without opening the data.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Description semantics match the claimed dataset type (prospective multimodal clinical cohort) and every technical term (OMOP CDM, WFDB, DICOM, Open mHealth, FLIO) is used correctly and consistently with conforms_to and file_collections.

sub_elements.name: Keywords or Tags for Searchability
sub_elements.evidence: keywords: [Diabetes mellitus, Machine Learning, Artificial Intelligence, Electrocardiography, Continuous Glucose Monitoring, Retinal imaging, Eye exam, Data Sharing, Exploratory Data Collection]
sub_elements.quality_note: Nine keywords spanning condition, methods and modalities; each one is actually realized in the release rather than aspirational.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Every keyword corresponds to content present in file_collections or variables (ECG, CGM, retinal imaging), so keyword-to-content semantics hold. Program context is inferable from funders.grantor (NIH Bridge2AI) rather than from the filename.

sub_elements.name: Landing Page and Resources (page, hierarchical resources)
sub_elements.evidence: page: https://fairhub.io/datasets/3; distribution_formats.access_urls includes https://fairhub.io/datasets/3/access; ten file_collections each with id, path, file_count, total_bytes and conforms_to; three subsets (public, controlled_access, mini_subset)
sub_elements.quality_note: A live platform landing page plus a fully enumerated internal resource hierarchy down to per-datatype counts and byte sizes.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: URLs are well formed on a plausible repository domain; the resource hierarchy matches the CDS v0.1.1 datatype/modality/device/participant layout described in preprocessing_strategies.

sub_elements.name: Hierarchical Structure (parent datasets, relationships)
sub_elements.evidence: related_datasets: is_new_version_of doi:10.60775/fairhub.2 and doi:10.60775/fairhub.1; is_described_by doi:10.1038/s42255-024-01165-x and doi:10.1136/bmjopen-2024-097449; subsets records the mini-subset as FAIRhub child dataset id 4
sub_elements.quality_note: Typed, DOI-bearing relationships in both directions (predecessor versions and describing publications) plus an explicit parent/child link to the mini-subset.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Relationship types are used correctly: version predecessors under is_new_version_of, journal articles under is_described_by with an explicit note that the targets are articles rather than datasets. Target DOI prefixes (10.1038 Nature, 10.1136 BMJ) match the named publishers.

elements.name: Dataset Access and Retrieval
elements.description: Can the dataset and its associated resources be located, accessed, and downloaded?

sub_elements.name: Access Policy and IP Restrictions Defined
sub_elements.evidence: license_and_use_terms.license_terms: 'AI-READI Data License Agreement, Version 2.0, with Washington University in St. Louis as Licensor (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.17555036)' with the grant of rights, the HIPAA-BAA storage restriction, treatment of derivative and synthetic data, and automatic termination on breach; data_use_permission: disease_specific_research; ip_restrictions: 'Title to the data, and all industrial and intellectual property rights therein, remain solely and exclusively with the Licensor'
sub_elements.quality_note: The operative terms are summarized at a level that lets an institution decide whether it can accept them, not merely named.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: License Zenodo DOI (10.5281 prefix, correct registrant for Zenodo) is well formed. Restrictiveness is consistent with regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level=restricted and with prohibited_uses; the three competing license names are disclosed rather than silently merged.

sub_elements.name: Regulatory Compliance and Confidentiality Classification
sub_elements.evidence: regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level: restricted; hipaa_compliant: compliant; regulatory_restrictions: NIH Genomic Data Sharing Policy security best practices, applicable-law compliance and static watermarking; other_compliance: not FDA-regulated (isFDARegulatedDrug/Device 'No'), no data monitoring committee, public release de-identified under HIPAA Safe Harbor; data_governance.access_review_process: 'PublicDownloadSelfAttestationRequired' with verified-ID login and DUA for the controlled tier
sub_elements.quality_note: Classification, the specific frameworks that apply (HIPAA, NIH GDS), the FDA status, and the access-review mechanism are all present and mutually coherent.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Two values are flagged by the record as derived rather than quoted (confidentiality_level versus the RO-Crate's 'HL7:2N (normal)'; hipaa_compliant with no source using that word) — disclosed derivation, counted as a warning not a failure. data_governance.committee_contact is unpopulated; contact routing appears only as prose (contact@aireadi.org in maintainers), a low-severity gap against the governance-contact scope of this sub-element.

sub_elements.name: Download URL or Platform Link Available
sub_elements.evidence: distribution_formats[0]: 'FAIRhub platform download with self-attestation' with access_urls https://fairhub.io/datasets/3 and https://fairhub.io/datasets/3/access; notes add that v3.0.0 documentation covers Azure Storage access and that 'All data files are in formats accessible with free software commonly used for such data types'; data_governance.notes records access conditions URL https://fairhub.io/datasets/3/access
sub_elements.quality_note: Actionable access route with the prerequisites stated (verified-ID login, T2DM-only use attestation, license agreement) and a named alternative transfer path via Azure Storage.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: The dedicated download_url slot is empty and the links live in distribution_formats.access_urls; scored on substance because the sub-element asks for a download or platform link and a working, qualified one is supplied. Recorded as a low-severity completeness issue rather than a scoring failure.

sub_elements.name: Distribution Formats and File Types Specified
sub_elements.evidence: distribution_formats entries for DICOM (application/dicom), CSV (text/csv), JSON (application/json) and Markdown (text/markdown), each with the in-release use stated; file_collections give per-datatype conforms_to_standard (WFDB, OMOP_CDM, ESDS, DICOM, OPEN_MHEALTH)
sub_elements.quality_note: Formats are given with MIME types and mapped to the specific content they carry, so a consumer knows which reader to bring to which directory.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Media types are correct for the named formats. Character encoding is not stated anywhere, a minor gap against the encoding scope; format coverage is otherwise complete for all nine datatype directories.

sub_elements.name: Related Datasets and External Resources Linked
sub_elements.evidence: related_datasets: four typed DOI-bearing links; external_resources: https://docs.aireadi.org with per-domain documentation and CC-BY 4.0 terms, https://aireadi.org plus team/goals/contact pages, https://zenodo.org/communities/aireadi, https://github.com/AI-READI, https://cds-specification.readthedocs.io/en/v0.1.1/
sub_elements.quality_note: Both prior versions and the describing literature are linked, and the external documentation entry states its own license and the consequence of an outage (the release is self-contained).
sub_elements.semantic_validation: All URLs are structurally valid on plausible domains; the CDS specification link pins the exact version (v0.1.1) asserted in conforms_to, so the standards claim is checkable.

elements.name: Data Reuse and Interoperability
elements.description: Is sufficient information provided to reuse and integrate the dataset with others?

sub_elements.name: License Terms Allow Reuse
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition met on E2 evidence: distribution_formats populated with FAIRhub access_urls, page https://fairhub.io/datasets/3 resolves to an accessible release, and the license explicitly permits commercial and research reuse and derivative works.
sub_elements.evidence: license_and_use_terms: custom license 'specifically tailored to enable reuse of the AI-READI dataset for commercial or research purposes'; grants a non-exclusive, non-transferable license to download, reproduce and use the data and to create derivative works; intended_uses permits distribution of models trained on the data that do not contain the data
sub_elements.quality_note: Reuse is affirmatively permitted, including commercially, with the boundaries drawn precisely enough to plan around (onward sharing only to co-licensees, five-figure publication cap, memorization-minimization duty).
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Permissions and restrictions are mutually consistent, and the disease-specific limit in data_use_permission matches the T2DM-only attestation in access_review_process and intended_uses.usage_notes.

sub_elements.name: Data Formats Are Standardized (encoding, format)
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same datasets-shared condition: E2 distribution_formats and an accessible FAIRhub landing page.
sub_elements.evidence: conforms_to_standard: [CDS, WFDB, OMOP_CDM, ESDS, DICOM, OPEN_MHEALTH, RO_CRATE]; distribution_formats give DICOM/CSV/JSON/Markdown with media types; each file_collection declares its own conforms_to (for example cardiac_ecg to WFDB, clinical_data one-to-one with OMOP CDM tables, wearable_blood_glucose to Open mHealth)
sub_elements.quality_note: Every modality lands in an open, community-standard container rather than a vendor format, and the record states that vendor formats were converted on the way in.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Format-to-modality assignments are semantically correct (WFDB for waveforms, DICOM for ophthalmic imaging, Open mHealth for wearables, ESDS for environmental time series). Character encoding is nowhere declared — the one unmet part of this sub-element's scope, insufficient to overturn otherwise exemplary format standardization.

sub_elements.name: Schema or Ontology Conformance Stated
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same datasets-shared condition: E2 distribution_formats and an accessible FAIRhub landing page.
sub_elements.evidence: conforms_to: CDS v0.1.1 layout with per-datatype standards, plus an RO-Crate metadata file conforming to RO-Crate 1.2-DRAFT and FAIRscape profile 0.1; conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema; conforms_to_class: Dataset
sub_elements.quality_note: Both the data-level standards and the metadata-level schema are pinned, with versions, so conformance is verifiable rather than asserted.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Named standards exist and are correctly characterized (OMOP CDM as an observational clinical model, ESDS as a NASA ASCII guideline for Earth science data); versions are specific (CDS v0.1.1, RO-Crate 1.2-DRAFT, FAIRscape 0.1).

sub_elements.name: Variable Metadata with Identifiers Defined
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same datasets-shared condition: E2 distribution_formats and an accessible FAIRhub landing page.
sub_elements.evidence: variables: eight substantive entries (HbA1c %, continuous blood glucose mg/dL, best-corrected visual acuity logMAR, letter contrast sensitivity, MoCA total score, systolic blood pressure mm Hg, step count, PM2.5) each with data_type, unit where applicable, measurement_technique naming the instrument and protocol, and quality_notes; plus a 'Representative subset marker' entry declaring the list partial and pointing to https://docs.aireadi.org
sub_elements.quality_note: The variable documentation that is present is unusually careful — it distinguishes laboratory reference ranges and instrument maxima from observed minima and maxima rather than mis-filing them, and gives acquisition detail sufficient to reproduce a measurement.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Units and data types are semantically correct for each measure. Two shortfalls are recorded as a medium-severity issue rather than a failure: no variable carries an ontology or concept identifier despite the OMOP mapping, and the inventory is self-declared incomplete with the full dictionary externalized.

sub_elements.name: Use Guidance Provided (intended, prohibited uses)
sub_elements.evidence: intended_uses: two categories with examples (pseudotime manifold analysis, multimodal model development) and usage_notes on the verified-ID and third-party-model-vendor BAA conditions; prohibited_uses: six specific prohibitions including no clinical treatment decisions, no re-identification or contact attempts, no sharing with model vendors for training, no onward transfer outside the licensee set, publication limited to five illustrative figures, and no watermark tampering
sub_elements.quality_note: Guidance is operational: a researcher can tell in advance whether a planned analysis, a planned collaboration and a planned figure are permitted.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Prohibitions are coherent with the privacy rationale in participant_privacy and future_use_impacts (re-identification risk from AI inference motivates the model-vendor and watermark clauses), so the guidance is semantically grounded rather than boilerplate. No discouraged_uses are stated, which the intended/prohibited pair covers adequately.

elements.name: Ethical Use and Privacy Safeguards
elements.description: Does the dataset provide clear information about consent, privacy, and ethical oversight?

sub_elements.name: IRB or Ethics Review and Data Protection Impact
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Human-subjects condition met on E1 and E8 evidence, not on E4's own fields: description reads '2,280 adults with and without type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM)' collected at three sites; keywords include 'Diabetes mellitus' and 'Eye exam'; collection_mechanisms (E8) describes EHR-based recruitment pools, REDCap e-consent and in-person study visits. The governance condition is independently met on E2 (confidentiality_level restricted, NIH GDS security requirements).
sub_elements.evidence: ethical_reviews[0]: University of Washington Institutional Review Board (Human Subjects Division), 'approved under IRB protocol STUDY00016228, with reliance agreements with the IRBs of the University of Alabama at Birmingham and the University of California, San Diego. Initial approval was received on December 20, 2022'; annual renewal due within 90 days of expiration; human_subject_research.ethics_review_board gives the full HSD address and the IRB reliance contact hsdrely@uw.edu; ethical_reviews[1] names four ELSI reviewers (Camille Nebeker, Debra Mathews, Kadija Ferryman, Nicholas Evans)
sub_elements.quality_note: Protocol number, approval date, multi-site reliance structure, renewal obligation and a named ethics contact — enough for a reader to verify oversight independently. A standing ELSI review function and Native Biodata Consortium engagement go beyond a single approval letter.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Passes the required check: involves_human_subjects=true is matched by populated ethics review. data_protection_impacts is absent as a field, though re-identification risk is assessed under participant_privacy — recorded as a low-severity gap. The reviewing-institution conflict (Washington University IRB per RO-Crate versus University of Washington per healthsheet and BMJ Open) is disclosed and the UW reading taken.

sub_elements.name: Deidentification Method Described
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same external evidence as sub-element 1: E1 description and keywords identify a human clinical cohort; E8 collection_mechanisms describes participant recruitment and visits; E2 regulatory_restrictions states an applying governance constraint (restricted, HIPAA, NIH GDS).
sub_elements.evidence: is_deidentified.method: 'No identifiers were collected, so no active de-identification was necessary... The public set is stripped of Protected Health Information as defined by the HIPAA Privacy Rule using the Safe Harbor method', with the FAIRhub flags recording direct identifier removal and HIPAA de-identification as applied and date shifting, non-arrangement of dates and k-anonymization as not applied; identifiers_removed: 'HIPAA Safe Harbor identifiers (Protected Health Information); Sex; Race and ethnicity; Medications used'; deidentification_details adds internal review for accidental PII
sub_elements.quality_note: A named method, an explicit list of what was removed, and an explicit list of techniques not used — the negative declarations are as informative as the positive ones for a re-identification risk assessor.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Safe Harbor is appropriate for this data type, and the extra removal of sex, race/ethnicity and medications to a controlled tier is consistent with subpopulations.subpopulation_elements_present=false and with the splits rationale. The 'NoDeIdentification' type alongside asserted Safe Harbor stripping is an internal tension, disclosed by the record and logged as a low-severity issue.

sub_elements.name: Privacy Protections and Re-identification Risk Assessment
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Participant-signal condition met on E1/E8 evidence: description names 2,280 adult participants with and without T2DM; collection_mechanisms (E8) describes device wear, home sensor placement and in-person visits. Applicability does not rest on the governance disjunct or on E4's own fields.
sub_elements.evidence: participant_privacy.anonymization_method (Safe Harbor plus removal of sex, race/ethnicity, medications); privacy_techniques: robust dissemination system, strict licence, static licensee watermarking, deliberate device selection ('these devices do not capture video or audio, are not equipped with GPS location monitoring and are not synced with participant-owned devices'), encrypted servers under Level 3 data security classification; reidentification_risk: 'theoretical risk of future re-identification... AI algorithms can infer individual patient characteristics and could facilitate individual-level identification'; data_linkage names the controlled-tier variables
sub_elements.quality_note: Risk is assessed rather than dismissed, and each protection is tied to the specific threat it addresses, including a design-time privacy decision about which sensors to deploy.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Passes the required check: a re-identification risk assessment exists and is mitigated. The assessed risk is proportionate to the data type (dense wearable and imaging data at three named sites), and the linkage disclosure correctly identifies the controlled tier as the residual risk surface.

sub_elements.name: Informed Consent Obtained from Participants
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Participant-signal condition met on E1/E8 evidence: E1 description identifies adult human participants; E8 collection_mechanisms records REDCap-hosted screening and electronic consent.
sub_elements.evidence: informed_consent.consent_obtained: true; consent_type: written, electronically via REDCap e-consent with a unique emailed code or in person at visit start; consent_scope: public version restricted to T2DM-related research, no non-commercial or geographic restriction, methods development not prohibited; consent_documentation names the approved UW form (Mod 17 May 2023) published with the v3.0.0 documentation and the UCSD Experimental Subject's Bill of Rights addendum; withdrawal_mechanism plus consent_revocations: data already shared 'would stay in the dataset. This limitation is clearly communicated in the consent document'
sub_elements.quality_note: Consent mechanics, scope, documentation location, and the honest limit of withdrawal are all stated — including collection_notifications confirming participants knew collection was active rather than passive.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Passes the required check pairing IRB approval with consent procedures. Consent scope (T2DM-only for the public tier, broader for controlled) is consistent with data_use_permission=disease_specific_research and with the access attestation, so the downstream license terms are traceable to what participants agreed to.

sub_elements.name: Vulnerable Populations and Compensation Documented
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Participant-signal condition met on E1/E8 evidence: E1 description identifies an adult human cohort; E8 collection_mechanisms and data_collectors describe recruitment, enrollment and study visits.
sub_elements.evidence: at_risk_populations.special_protections: minors excluded (40-85 eligibility), pregnancy and gestational diabetes as exclusions, rideshare and parking/transit cost coverage for participants endorsing transport barriers, with a source_caveat explaining why at_risk_groups_included is left unset; participant_compensation: compensation_provided true, 200 US dollars, stipend funded through the grant, with notes that payment follows device return (typically two weeks post-visit), is not prorated, may change with funding, and that transport costs above 25 dollars are unreimbursed
sub_elements.quality_note: Compensation is documented to the level of disbursement timing, prorating and its stated shortfall — the kind of detail an IRB reviewer or a participant advocate would actually ask for.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Exclusion-based protections are coherent with human_subject_research.special_populations (same 40-85 range, same pregnancy and type 1 exclusions). The record declines to assert an at_risk_groups_included boolean the sources do not support, which is correct restraint rather than an omission.

elements.name: Data Composition and Structure
elements.description: Can the dataset's structure, modality, and population be understood from metadata?

sub_elements.name: Cohort or Subpopulations Characteristics Described
sub_elements.evidence: subpopulations.distribution: 'by race/ethnicity, Hispanic 380, Asian 545, Black 519, white 836; by sex, male 951, female 1,329; by diabetes status, no diabetes 776, lifestyle-controlled 560, oral-medication-controlled 686, insulin-controlled 258. Mean age across the cohort is 60.8 years with a standard deviation of 11.3'; identification explains that per-instance demographic labels are withheld to the controlled tier; eligibility (40-85, English-speaking, pregnancy/gestational/type 1 excluded) in human_subject_research.special_populations and known_limitations
sub_elements.quality_note: Cohort-level demographics are quantified, inclusion and exclusion criteria are explicit, and the reason per-instance labels are absent is stated rather than left as a silent hole.

sub_elements.semantic_validation: All links are structurally valid and version-scoped where relevant (docs.aireadi.org/docs/3/...), so a user reaches documentation for this release rather than for a different version.

sub_elements.name: Related Datasets with Typed Relationships
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same datasets-shared condition (E2 distribution_formats and accessible landing page).
sub_elements.evidence: related_datasets: is_new_version_of doi:10.60775/fairhub.2 and doi:10.60775/fairhub.1 with participant, file and size figures for each; is_described_by doi:10.1038/s42255-024-01165-x (Nature Metabolism comment) and doi:10.1136/bmjopen-2024-097449 (BMJ Open protocol) with full bibliographic detail; subsets records the mini-subset as FAIRhub child id 4
sub_elements.quality_note: Relationships are typed, DOI-resolvable and annotated with what the target contains and, for v2.0.0, that it is no longer accessible.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Relationship types are semantically apt, and the record flags that two is_described_by targets are journal articles rather than datasets, choosing the relationship the source attests rather than forcing a dataset-only reading — correct use of a typed vocabulary under imperfect fit.

strengths: Provenance discipline is exceptional: eleven numbered source_caveats at the record root plus per-field caveats disclose every disagreement between tier-1 sources (project-name expansion, accountable organization, IRB name, enrollment start, target enrollment, file counts, directory sizes, release scope, follow-up fraction, license name, roster detail) and state the tie-break rule applied, so a reader can audit each choice rather than inherit it.

Internal arithmetic is verifiable and almost entirely correct: datatype file counts sum to 356,334 and reconcile to 356,343 via the nine root metadata files; participant strata sum to 2,280 across race/ethnicity, sex and diabetes status; and all three recommended splits' strata sum to their sizes.

Ethics and privacy documentation is complete end to end and mutually consistent — IRB protocol STUDY00016228 with approval date and multi-site reliance, REDCap e-consent with the withdrawal limit stated plainly, HIPAA Safe Harbor with an explicit list of what was and was not applied, an AI-specific re-identification risk assessment, and privacy-motivated device selection (no audio, video or GPS).

Collection and acquisition methods are documented at replication-grade specificity: per-device scan patterns, fields of view, body position during ECG, wear durations, laboratory shipping and assay routing, and a named data-entry verification procedure.

Interoperability is designed rather than claimed: seven community standards bound to the specific content that conforms to each, OMOP CDM one-to-one table mapping, version-pinned CDS v0.1.1 structure, and an RO-Crate metadata file for machine consumption.

Limitations and biases are typed, quantified where possible, and each paired with a mitigation that is genuinely responsive, including a recommended split whose validation and test sets are balanced on the very attributes withheld from the public tier.

Version history is complete and honest: three DOI-bearing releases with counts and sizes, an explicit statement that v2.0.0 is no longer accessible, and a breaking change (Snellen variables dropped) surfaced both in version_details and in known_limitations.
weaknesses: No software is named that produced or transformed the distributed data: the .fda/.sdt-to-DICOM, .FIT-to-Open-mHealth and ECG-to-WFDB conversions are described without a tool, and no used_software is attached to any strategy — the only scoring deduction in the evaluation.

Accountable organization remains unresolved: Washington University in St. Louis is recorded as governance-accountable and Licensor while the University of Washington is recorded as the reviewing IRB and PI affiliation, so the datasheet asserts both readings in different slots.

Variable documentation is self-declared incomplete and carries no ontology or concept identifiers, despite the clinical data being mapped one-to-one to OMOP CDM tables — the full dictionary is reachable only as a prose pointer to docs.aireadi.org.

Two governance enum values (confidentiality_level 'restricted', hipaa_compliant 'compliant') are inferences rather than source attestations, as the record itself states, and the RO-Crate's own classification is 'HL7:2N (normal)'.
Dedicated slots are left empty where the information exists in prose: download_url, data_governance.committee_contact, data_protection_impacts, and character encoding for the distributed formats.
The per-directory byte totals fall 419,614 bytes short of the reported total_size_bytes, an unexplained arithmetic discrepancy carried from the source.
recommendations: Name the processing software with versions and attach it via used_software on the relevant preprocessing_strategies entries — specifically the converters that produced DICOM from Topcon .fda and Heidelberg .sdt, Open mHealth from Garmin .FIT, and WFDB from the Philips ECG export — with repository or software-DOI links under the AI-READI GitHub organization rather than the organization root alone.

Resolve the licensor and IRB-of-record attribution with the consortium and state one accountable organization for governance, keeping the source disagreement as a caveat rather than as divergent values in adjacent slots.

Attach OMOP concept identifiers or LOINC codes to the clinical and laboratory variables and publish the full machine-readable data dictionary per domain, so variable-level integration does not depend on reading a documentation site.

Populate download_url, data_governance.committee_contact (contact@aireadi.org is already in maintainers) and data_protection_impacts from information already present in prose, and declare character encoding for the text-based distribution formats.

Reconcile the per-directory byte totals with total_size_bytes, or state what the 419,614-byte residual accounts for, and add a one-line statement that no statistical imputation was performed so the imputation scope is answered explicitly rather than by inference.

Name the conversion and standardization software with versions and attach it via used_software on preprocessing_strategies; link the AI-READI processing code repositories rather than the GitHub organization root.
State a single accountable organization for data governance and reconcile it with the IRB-of-record and PI affiliation, retaining the source conflict as a caveat.
Add OMOP concept or LOINC identifiers to variables and publish the full per-domain data dictionary in machine-readable form.
Populate download_url, data_governance.committee_contact and data_protection_impacts from the values already present in prose, and declare character encoding for text formats.
Reconcile the per-directory byte totals with total_size_bytes and state explicitly that no statistical imputation was performed.
